name: Migrate a WordPress, Elementor or Shopify site to Next.js with MiroMiro

parameters.content:
## Migrate a WordPress, Elementor or Shopify site to Next.js with MiroMiro

### How it works
Migrate the pages of a live site (WordPress, Elementor, Shopify, Webflow, anything public) to a Next.js + Tailwind project. **List Pages to Migrate** holds each URL and the route it becomes. **Extract Hero and Find Sections** reads each page in a real browser and lists its sections, **Extract Each Section as React** rebuilds every one as a component, and **Assemble Next.js Project** puts them in page order into an App Router project with Tailwind 4. A section that fails is skipped and counted in `failed`. Failed calls are not charged.

### Setup
This template uses the verified community node **n8n-nodes-miromiro** (tested with version 0.1.4 on n8n 1.123).
1. On n8n Cloud, search "MiroMiro" in the nodes panel (an admin may need to turn on Verified Community Nodes). Self-hosted: Settings > Community nodes > Install `n8n-nodes-miromiro`, see https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/community-nodes/installation/
2. Get a free MiroMiro API key (300 credits a month, no card): https://miromiro.app/api/onboarding
3. Open **Extract Hero and Find Sections** > Credential > Create new, and paste the key.
4. Select the same credential in **Extract Each Section as React**.
5. List your pages in **List Pages to Migrate** and click **Execute workflow**.
6. Download the zip from **Zip the Next.js Project**, then run `npm install` and `npm run dev`.

Each section costs 10 credits, so a page of 6 to 12 sections is 60 to 120. The same page again within 24 hours is free.

### Customization
Push the files to GitHub instead of zipping them. Before launch: replace the source site's text and images unless it is yours, wire up menus, sliders and forms (they arrive as static markup), and load the fonts.

![The workflow, in case the preview does not load](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SoraiaBarroso/n8n-nodes-miromiro/main/docs/templates/migrate-site-to-nextjs.png)

## List the pages

One line per page in **List Pages to Migrate**: the live URL and its Next.js route.

## Find the sections

The first call rebuilds each page's hero and lists its other sections.

## Rebuild and assemble

Each section becomes a React component. Failed ones are skipped and counted; the rest become a zipped Next.js project.
